tasks.short: Review spatial data quality and documentation

steps.what: Identify incoming data versions, stated currency and the applicable quality requirements
outputs: verified dataset identity and check specification

steps.what: Check data dates, required fields, geometry validity and documentation presence
inputs: verified dataset identity and check specification
outputs: fixed validation results and unresolved fields

steps.what: Read the documentation and assess data usefulness and stated limitations
inputs: fixed validation results and unresolved fields

steps.what: Inspect actual data samples for accuracy and quality beyond fixed checks
Write the actual data review findings, usefulness limits and unresolved concerns
inputs: fixed validation results and unresolved fields

steps.what: Save the data review in its existing working file

tasks.design: Configure native validation in the GIS tool {OTHER} for dates, schemas, geometry and required metadata, with a reusable findings format in {DOCS}. The technician still reads documentation, samples actual data and judges fitness for the intended use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fixed validation checks are repeated manually alongside substantive data review.
tasks.enabler_now: Native validators can produce traceable fixed-check results without inferring real-world accuracy.
tasks.still_hard: Valid geometry and present metadata do not prove currency, accuracy or usefulness.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when technically valid data would mislead the intended analysis.

ambition.what: Fitness-for-use judgement remains with the technician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS validators can check fixed geometry and metadata rules while real-world quality and usefulness require contextual review.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing GIS desktop and dataset catalogue. Boundary is the actual quality review used by the data team, not data acceptance, publication or an invented additional report.

Data providers supply dataset version, schema, reference system, dates and documentation; s1 counts technician identification and rule selection. Missing or incompatible metadata stays flagged and needs funded manual repair.
s2 replaces actual manual fixed checks. s5 removes1.9 units of repeated finding headings, retaining17.1 for actual conclusions and checks. Native validation already active earns no new labour saving.
All45 substantive documentation and visual review units remain. The ordinary one-unit author save is fully retained and ungated; no self-approval of findings is introduced.
unknowns: Current manual validation and metadata completeness
research_questions: Can validation distinguish a missing date from evidence that data is current?

already_counted.description: Identify inputs, read documentation, inspect samples, write actual findings and save

incremental.description: Maintain validation rules and manually resolve missing metadata or failed checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R73.1 gross26.9 less upkeep4 gives22.9. For legacy layers without reliable currency metadata, fixed checking retains20 of25 while the findings format still retains17.1 of19; identity10, documentation25, samples20 and save1 remain. Gross6.9 less upkeep4 gives2.9. No semantic quality judgement or ordinary saving is removed.

tasks.short: Produce spatial layers, maps and tables

steps.what: Specify the required spatial analysis, source layers and output meaning
Stage the specified data layers and map their existing reference and field definitions
Set up the specified spatial procedures and assemble their resulting layers and tables
Lay out the required maps, tables or reports with actual output labels
Inspect the produced layers, maps and tables for spatial meaning and analysis errors
Save the produced maps and data layers in the existing project

tasks.design: Use native GIS processing models in {OTHER} to stage specified compatible layers and repeat the technician's chosen spatial procedure chain. Reuse the actual map layout while retaining specification, meaningful label work and full visual and analytical checking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Layer staging, repeated tool setup and output layout are manually repeated for comparable requests.
tasks.enabler_now: Native processing models and layout templates remove repeated operator setup without choosing the analysis.
tasks.still_hard: The right reference system, spatial relationship and interpretation depend on the request and source limitations.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an apparently plausible map whose analysis or meaning is wrong.

ambition.what: Analysis design and output interpretation remain with the technician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS processing models can repeat specified layer staging and tool setup, with analytical design and output checking retained.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing GIS processing and mapping tool. Boundary is internal production of the actual requested outputs, not public map publication or a production database update.

Data owners supply layer ids, fields, reference systems and versions. s1 counts the technician's request interpretation, field mapping and exact operation and parameter specification. Missing or incompatible layers require funded manual repair.

s2 replaces actual manual layer staging and s3 repeated operator parameter entry and result assembly. Existing spatial calculation runtime is already automatic and earns zero labour saving; no CPU waiting is priced as operator work.
s4 removes six units of repeated legend, frame and table layout, retaining nine for output-specific labels and checks. Native models and templates already used earn no new saving.
All44 specification and substantive checking units remain. The ordinary one-unit project save is fully retained and ungated, without author self-approval.
research_questions: Can a repeated model expose source versions and parameters so output meaning can be verified?

already_counted.description: Specify analysis, finish actual output labels, inspect meaning and save

incremental.description: Maintain models and layouts and repair incompatible layer or parameter mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R54 gross46 less upkeep6 gives40. With mixed layer definitions and an unusual output layout, staging retains17 of20, procedure setup15 of20 and layout14 of15; specification20, checking24 and save1 remain. R91 gross9 less upkeep6 gives3. Existing calculation runtime and ordinary saving supply no benefit.

steps.what: Verify the requested Geographic Information Systems database change and affected data
inputs: current database schema and source data
outputs: verified change scope and field mapping

steps.what: Prepare the actual GIS database edits in staging and inspect the proposed difference
inputs: verified change scope and field mapping
current database schema and source data

steps.what: Check the staged GIS database changes against fixed schema, topology and reference rules
Review the final GIS database difference and authorise its production application
inputs: verified change scope and field mapping

steps.what: Apply only the authorised GIS database difference to the production database
Verify the changed GIS database through actual queries and spatial inspection
inputs: verified change scope and field mapping

tasks.design: Use native staged editing and batch field rules in the GIS database tool {OTHER}, with fixed validation of the complete proposed difference. The database owner reviews that version before production application, and the technician verifies actual query and spatial behaviour afterward.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated row edits and fixed validation are manually performed around controlled database maintenance.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch editors and validators remove repeated entry and rule checking without approving production changes.
tasks.still_hard: A structurally valid edit can still have the wrong spatial meaning or affect dependent users.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the requested change and detect downstream semantic errors.

ambition.what: Change interpretation and database authority remain human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native staged database edits and fixed GIS validation can reduce repeated maintenance work while production authorisation and semantic verification remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing spatial database and GIS editing tools. Boundary is an actual production data change with its established database-owner authority, not an ordinary save of the technician's own document.

Requesters supply the intended change; data owners supply existing schema and source values. s1 counts interpretation and field mapping; s2 counts actual staged content and difference checking. No ready-made clean edit is assumed free.

s2 removes12 units of repeated row and field entry, retaining18 for actual changes and inspection. s3 replaces manual fixed schema, topology and reference checks, with funded manual repair for incompatible rules or values.
Native batch tools and validators are tested before code, and existing runtime earns no saving. All24 post-change query and spatial checks remain.

s4 is the real database owner's final production authority after the complete difference and tests exist. The gate binds source version, exact difference and target database; changes or source drift void it. The one-unit operative commit remains fully retained. Ordinary staging saves are negligible and ungated.
unknowns: Actual owner and production change route
Repeatable row edits and validation rules
research_questions: Can source-version drift invalidate the approved difference before production application?

already_counted.description: Verify scope, prepare actual edits, apply the authorised difference and check production behaviour
Existing database owner reviews the final production difference

incremental.description: Maintain edit and validation rules and manually repair incompatible data or failed checks

approvals.approved_version: Exact staged difference, source version, validation results and production target authorised in s4; edits or source drift void authority

Seven focal units saved over90 gives7.777 less upkeep5=2.777; low2.7. Owner review and commit runtime earn no saving.

steps.what: Understand the information and audience before selecting cartographic elements
Compare and select cartographic symbols, classification and visual hierarchy
Apply the selected cartographic elements to the working presentation
Inspect whether the cartographic presentation communicates the information effectively
Save the chosen cartographic elements in the existing working project

tasks.design: Reuse native style presets in the GIS tool {OTHER} for applying the technician's chosen elements. The technician chooses symbols, classification and hierarchy from the actual information and audience needs and checks the visual result.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chosen symbol settings are repeatedly entered during presentation preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native style presets remove repeated settings without deciding which cartographic treatment is appropriate.
tasks.still_hard: A visually tidy map can mislead through classification, scale or emphasis.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a truthful and legible visual treatment for the actual audience.

ambition.what: Cartographic selection remains the technician's judgement.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native GIS style presets reduce repeated setting entry while effective cartographic selection requires visual judgement.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing GIS mapping and style tool. Boundary is selecting and applying working cartographic elements, not external map publication or a new style-selection report.

The requester supplies the presentation purpose and source owners supply actual data. s1 and s2 count technician interpretation and selection; no structured communication brief or automatic palette choice is presumed free.

s3 removes1.9 units of repeated symbol settings, retaining17.1 for applying the actual choices and adjustments. All80 purpose, selection and visual-check units remain. Existing style presets already used earn no new benefit.
The ordinary one-unit working-project save is fully retained and ungated. No author self-approval or formal release is added.
research_questions: Can the preset preserve chosen classification and labels without hiding misleading emphasis?

already_counted.description: Understand purpose, choose elements, apply and visually check them and save

incremental.description: Maintain the small style preset collection
